title: Bonebrake v. Cox — predominant purpose
summary: A sale and installation of bowling equipment was analyzed as predominantly a goods transaction.
notes:
Casebook discussion of a shorter authority.

The test asks whether services predominate with goods incidental, or goods predominate with labor incidental. The book gives examples of a painting commission and installing a water heater to illustrate the classification.

sources.label: Farnsworth et al., Contracts: Cases and Materials, 10th ed. (2023), pp. 249. Open assigned page 249.
